method.method_draft: First identify the Cu/Cu+ side from the image as the left half-cell connected by a NaBr salt bridge. Use the displayed overall reaction to see that Cu+ is being reduced to Cu(s) in that left half-cell. Because Cu+ cations are removed from solution there, the Cu half-cell develops an excess of negative charge from spectator anions. To neutralize this, cations from the salt bridge flow into the Cu/Cu+ half-cell; in NaBr, the cation is Na+, so Na+ flows to the Cu/Cu+ half-cell.
